summary: A case study, drawn by core's case-study view.

root.note: Inside the document skeleton page.json draws once (section#landmarks).

children.when: the index has a safe href

children.note: The story column (SC-036): the hero image and the narrative, in reading order, capped at the reading measure whether or not the aside is drawn. With no part to draw, as for a case study with only a title, no story is drawn, so no empty wrapper.
The hero image: the featured image, the story's first part, in either header variant. It is the view's priority image, the only one (section#priority-media).

children.when: caseStudyImage resolves to a media item other than the featured image
children.note: The case-study image in the flow (SC-034): always after the challenge's place and before the solution's, so with no challenge it follows the header, and with no solution it comes before the gallery. It keeps that place when the challenge, the solution or the featured image is absent: it is never promoted to the hero, and nothing is drawn in its place when it is absent or does not resolve. When it resolves to the same media item as the featured image (the same media identity, such as the same WordPress attachment ID, never compared by alt text or file name), it is drawn once, in the hero, and not here.

Never the priority image, so lazy. Not framed: it keeps its own proportion at the content width, uncropped, its width and height reserving the space (primitives.css). Its alt by the media's normal rules (media.json). No caption.

data-columns.when: two or fewer, or four or more

children.when: a part of the story is drawn
a detail, the client, the sector or a service is drawn
children.note: The project's facts beside the story from 64rem, after it below 64rem (SC-036). Only rows with a value are drawn, and with none the aside is not drawn at all, so the article keeps no empty track.

children.when: the client's name is not empty

children.note: The client's name: the chosen client record's title when the site enables clients and the record resolves, otherwise the free-text client (SC-035). Never a link.

children.when: the sector's name is not empty

children.note: The sector's name, by the client's rule: the chosen sector record's title when the site enables sectors and the record resolves, otherwise the free-text sector (SC-035). Never a link.

One dd per delivered service the document holds, in its order: the service's title, a link when the service has a public page (its href), plain text when it has none. A service with no public page that may still be shown is drawn plain; one that may not be shown (on WordPress, not published) is not in the document, so is not drawn.

data-tone-dark.note: site.caseStudy.headerToneDark, or the tone itself when that is unset, written server-side as a section's is.

children.when: the index has a safe href

band.note: The header drawn as section.json draws a band, so the tone's roles all reach it: salt-section with the tones, md spacing (which sections.css turns into the band's block space) and the default width, and its parts inside div.salt-section__content. It is the article's first row, above the story and the aside (SC-036): its content keeps their left edge and the width they span, and the tone's background bleeds to both viewport edges.

variants.note: plain draws the base tree. band wraps the header's parts in a content div, so the order differs from plain's.

headings.children: section headings h2; their bodies from base 2

hooks.reason: Tells the client's row from a project detail's, for a site's own styles and for conformance; the row is styled as every detail is, through salt-case-study-view__detail's parts.
Groups each dt with its dd or dds, a detail's, the client's, the sector's or the services'; the details grid styles the pair's parts.
The live-site link's paragraph; the button carries the rules.
Each of the three content sections (challenge, solution, gallery); the view's rules space its heading and parts as children of it, and it has no rule of its own.
Tells the sector's row from a project detail's, for a site's own styles and for conformance; the row is styled as every detail is, through salt-case-study-view__detail's parts.
Tells the delivered services' row from a project detail's, for a site's own styles and for conformance; the row is styled as every detail is, through salt-case-study-view__detail's parts.

notes.text: This view's vocabulary is core's and fixed here, because primitives.css styles it.
primitives.css mentions .salt-case-study only in a comment (a site's own older copy); it is not contract vocabulary.

The hero and the flow (SC-034). The featured image is the hero image, drawn first in the story column below the header, in either header variant, and it is the view's only priority image. caseStudyImage is a separate optional image, drawn in the flow between the challenge and the solution and never the priority image. Neither is ever drawn in the other's place, neither leaves an empty wrapper, and one media item is never drawn twice. The image aside goes: no image runs beside the view's parts, and nothing in the markup counts them. Only the image aside is removed: the aside the view draws is of the project's facts, never an image (SC-036).

The header, the story and the aside (SC-036). The article's first row is the header: the back link, the title and the summary, across the width the story and the aside span below it. Then the story column holds the hero image, the challenge, the case-study image, the solution, the results, the gallery and the live-site link; the aside holds the project details, then the client, the sector and the delivered services, each only when it has a value, a service a link only to its own public page. The aside starts beside the story, never beside the title. Nothing appears in both: the header draws no client line, results or details, and no service cards are drawn. From 64rem the aside sits to the story's right, and the header puts the back link on its own line above the title, on its left edge, with the title and the summary side by side below it; with no back link no line is kept for it. Narrower, the aside follows the story and the header's lines stack, the hero reading as the header's last line, inside a band's tone. The story is capped at --container-2xl in either case, and the aside is --container-2xs.

owes: The featured image drawn first in the story column, as the priority image, and caseStudyImage (an attachment ID) drawn in div.salt-case-study-view__flow-media between the challenge and the solution, lazy, and not at all when it is the featured image's attachment (SC-034). No data-media or data-aside-rows on the article.
The section heading ids case-study__challenge-heading, case-study__solution-heading and case-study__gallery-heading, each named by its section's aria-labelledby (SC-012).

The header row, the story column and the aside (SC-036): the hero image moved into the story, the results and the details moved, the client line and the services section gone; Client and Sector from the record's title when its module is on and the record resolves, otherwise the free text; a service linked only when it is published and has a permalink, drawn plain when it has no public page, and left out when it may not be shown; the labels details, client and sector, with translators' comments.

The featured image drawn first in the story column, as the priority image, and caseStudyImage drawn in div.salt-case-study-view__flow-media between the challenge and the solution, lazy, and not at all when it is the featured image's media item; the media prop and its image aside layout go, with data-media, the aside rows and the measure (SC-034).
The header band's spacing from data-spacing alone, with no inline --salt-section-space (SC-029).

Name its three sections: the ids case-study__challenge-heading, case-study__solution-heading and case-study__gallery-heading on their h2s, and aria-labelledby on each section (section#labelled-by, SC-012).

The header row, the story column and the aside (SC-036), as Salt for WordPress owes them; the services' cards go, and each story image declares the story slot contract/image-sizes.json gives for whether the aside is drawn.
